governance.attested_by: neiso-50 head-repro session 2026-07-06 (confirmation re-solve + keeper swap, branch claude/neiso-49-resolve-confirm-7eb00b)
governance.note: neiso-50 = the IDENTICAL 2026-07-06-neiso-49-stgas-netload keeper recipe (same run_config, same reliability-floor CSV, same offer bands, same flags: --commitment --reliability-floor --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily --scarcity-price-overlay --tranche-startup-amortization), re-solved on today's main HEAD (dd85d5a) instead of the prior keeper's dirty, never-committed working tree. NO mechanism, offer band, or floor coefficient changed. This promotion is a REPRODUCIBILITY fix, not a structural or residual-fitting change: a session-level confirmation re-solve (neiso-49-resolve-confirm-7eb00b) found that 2026-07-06-neiso-49-stgas-netload's registered numbers rested on uncommitted local edits to scripts/run_calibration.py (git.dirty=true at solve time, listed but never captured as a diff) that produced a genuine NEISO zonal price separation (HQ_import pricing $0.31-$1.86/MWh below the mainland zones across 2023-2025). A git bisection across every commit between the keeper's base commit (ac11191) and today's HEAD -- including a CLEAN checkout of ac11191 itself with none of that session's dirty edits applied -- shows uniform system-wide pricing (zero HQ_import separation) at every single point in committed history. The separation was never reproducible from git; it only existed in that one solve session's WIP state. Mechanically this is expected, not a bug: under the scalar/measured-schedule interchange treatment NEISO uses (priced_interchange=False), HQ_import carries zero load (load_share=0.0) and zero generation, so its energy-balance row is a costless pass-through with nothing forcing net flow -- it can only mirror the system price. This has been true, and documented, since the very first NEISO smoke calibration (docs/calibration-log.md, 2026-06-12 entry: 'no Boston/CT congestion separation... TTC seeds are non-binding'), which also found that the alternative (--priced-interchange, which DOES route flow through HQ_import's real TTC-limited links) over-imports badly at the current static tranche prices (-23.5 TWh vs -10.3 actual in the 2024 diagnostic) -- so re-enabling it now specifically to chase this number back down would be exactly the 'reach the right number through a mechanism that isn't real' rule-1 violation this repo forbids. The honest, reproducible C3a price-mean level is worse than the prior registered figure by roughly the lost separation (2023 -8.3% -> -10.4%; 2024 -7.8% -> -8.6%; 2025 -1.6% -> -4.4%), on top of the already-ledgered, unrelated 0c6c833 offer-band de-leak gap below. C1 fuel-mix and C3b price-shape are unchanged to within reproducibility noise (<0.15% and 3rd-decimal NRMSE respectively). KNOWN GAP, owner-accepted: this promotion does NOT carry a freshly-solved zero-forcing ablation twin (CLAUDE.md rule 20/D-3) -- the owner explicitly deferred it pending the C3a determination check. 2026-07-06-neiso-49-stgas-netload's ablation twin bundle is being retired alongside the keeper it validated and is no longer a valid twin for this bundle (different, unreproducible base price level). A fresh ablation twin should be solved and registered as a follow-up before this keeper is considered fully rule-20-compliant.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage — per-class actuals are incomplete (audit 2026-07-04: 13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting; gas family incomplete). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which INCLUDES geothermal+biomass (~5.2 TWh); the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue documented for the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. When the full 2025 vintage reconciles, the per-class gate replaces this family fallback. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The post-solve ORDC scarcity overlay (ISO-NE-grounded LOLP curve: VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW ~ Millstone 3, sigma 900 MW = PAF Study 2022) fires and modifies econ_prices for capacity economics but does not change the persisted LP prices. The fast-start tranche pricing added in this run lifts the summer-evening and shoulder peak pricing but cannot produce >$300 cold-snap hours — that scarcity rent is the finite winter fuel INVENTORY the LP prices as an unlimited flow. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (docs/multi-iso/neiso-winter-fuel-inventory-plan-2026-07.md), NEVER via an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The fast-start tranche pricing + econ-band re-anchor recovered a third of the gap ENDOGENOUSLY (0.74 -> 1.05 TWh, no storage-formulation change — per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis, the PS number may only move downstream of price structure). The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Closes with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob. DEEPENED by neiso-49 (honest cost, rule #1): the measured-cost ST_GAS committed tranche shaves the artificial evening peak the PS fleet was arbitraging; the residual spread is the same ledgered winter/scarcity price-formation gap, and per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis it may only be recovered via price structure, never a storage knob.

entries.identification: derived-dependency (declares a coupling within already-counted scalars; not a new free parameter)
entries.source: The ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 and CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 bands are the NEISO-native CAMPD-measured marginal heat rate (ST_GAS 0.642/0.692/0.731; CC_CHP flat 0.94-0.97) multiplied by the NEISO-native CC reach ratio 1.223 (= CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 / native CC marginal HR 0.940). CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 is itself residual-identified (see the first ledger entry's offer_curve_by_group.value.CC_REGULAR.econ_high). So while the ST_GAS/CC_CHP bands are measured-grounded in level, the reach ratio that anchors them to the CC_REGULAR scale is not independent of that residual value.
